The committee convened to receive the final report of the independent review panel established after the disturbances at the municipal depot last autumn. The chair reminded members that the panel's terms of reference required it to examine not only the conduct of individual officers but also the adequacy of the policies, training procedures and supervisory arrangements that were in force at the time of the incidents. The report, which runs to two hundred and forty pages and is accompanied by a further volume of exhibits, concludes that the failures identified were systemic rather than attributable to any single individual. In particular, the panel found that the schedule of inspections had not been reviewed since the reorganization of the department in the previous decade, and that staffing levels at the depot had fallen by nearly a third while the volume of traffic passing through it had almost doubled. Witnesses who gave evidence in private described a working environment in which routine irregularities had become normalized and in which staff were reluctant to record concerns for fear that doing so would be treated as disloyalty. The panel recommends that the department adopt a written escalation procedure within six months, that all supervisory staff receive refresher training in the recognition of fatigue-related error, and that an annual external audit be published in full. It further recommends that the current practice of informal verbal authorization be replaced by a documented system requiring the signature of at least two responsible officers. Members noted that the financial implications of these recommendations had not been fully costed, and the finance director undertook to provide an estimate before the next meeting. Several members expressed concern that the timetable proposed by the panel was unrealistic given the department's existing workload, and a motion to extend the implementation period to twelve months was carried by seven votes to four. A minority statement submitted by two members argued that the panel had given insufficient weight to the evidence of the depot's own supervisors, whose account of the pressure under which they were operating differed materially from that of the complainant. The committee agreed to append the statement to the minutes without adopting its conclusions, and to invite the panel chair to respond in writing before the council considers the matter. The chair closed the meeting by observing that the report would be referred to the full council at its next session and that a further report on progress would be expected within one year. Copies of the minutes and of the panel's summary findings are to be circulated to all heads of service and placed on the public register in accordance with the council's transparency policy.
